title: Launch stress probe and ownership boarding
body:
Purpose:
This working doc captures a compact, actionable set of stress probes, KPIs to watch during the first 48–72 hours of a staged launch, and an ownership boarding sheet for each signal. Goal: reduce decision latency and avoid churn during a phased traffic ramp.

Status notes (quick):
- Drafted after last retro (2024-09-28) where we missed a cascading cache invalidation.
- Target for playbook signoff: engineering + ops by 2024-11-05.
- Scope: Host API + Dedicated rollout (canary -> 25% -> 100%). Not covering Private deployment cutover.

How to use this doc:
1) Before canary: owners confirm their instrumented dashboards and pager rotations.
2) During canary: run stress probes in parallel with controlled synthetic traffic.
3) If a gate fires: follow the short circuit in the "Immediate actions" section, escalate according to "Escalation ladder."

Quick links (preflight):
- Perf dashboards: /dashboards/launch/latency-aggregate (make sure you have access)
- Canary script: github.com/redwood-inference/launch-scripts/actions/run-canary
- Postmortem template: confluence:PLAT-Postmortem-Template

Key signals and owners (boarding table):
Metric | Baseline | Yellow threshold | Red threshold | Owner | Immediate action
---|---|---|---|---|---
P50 latency (in prod route) | 60ms | +25% (>=75ms) | +50% (>=90ms) | Priya Nair | Yellow: ENABLE single-tenant fast-path; Red: divert new traffic to fallback model
P95 latency | 190ms | +10% | +30% | Liam O'Neill | Yellow: reduce batch windows by 25%; Red: rollback new config
Error rate (5xx / minute) | 0.02% | 0.2% | 1.0% | Diego Alvarez | Yellow: increase concurrency limit; Red: pause route and notify SRE
Token cost per request (USD) | 0.003 | +20% | +50% | Maya Chen | Yellow: switch to lower-quant model for low-priority traffic; Red: trigger billing alert and rollback
Queue depth (requests waiting) | 4 | >20 | >100 | Samira Khan | Yellow: scale workers; Red: execute emergency capacity-scale runbook
Model quality regressions (eval set F1) | 0.87 | delta -0.02 | delta -0.05 | Research-oncall | Yellow: tag failing prompts, reduce traffic to model variant; Red: rollback model version

Rolling monitoring buckets (what to check every 10m during canary):
- Ingress throughput (rps) by route and customer tier
- Latency buckets (p50/p95/p99) per model variant
- Error codes breakdown (5xx vs 4xx vs model_decode errors)
- Resource saturation (GPU util, CPU steal, RAM) on serving pods
- Cost burn rate projection vs expected for the next 24h

Stress probes (automated & manual):
- Synthetic prefix-heavy traffic: simulate long-context traces to exercise KV cache and verify eviction behavior. Run for 15m at 2x baseline canary load. Owner: Priya.
- Small-burst bombard (cold-start mix): 1000 concurrent short requests to probe autoscaler reaction and queue behavior. Owner: Liam.
- Mixed-priority traffic shift: re-weight 10% of high-priority customer traffic to test routing policy. Owner: Diego.
- Gradual quantized performance test: serve a subset with quantized model to validate quality delta at scale. Owner: Research-oncall.

Immediate actions (short checklist to execute when a threshold hits red):
- Step 1: Gate traffic at load balancer to previous stable canary image. (Owner: SRE on call)
- Step 2: Set internal incident channel (#launch-ops) and update public status if customer-facing. (Owner: Ops lead)
- Step 3: Snapshot metrics + logs and mark them in linked_artifacts with timestamps. (Owner: whoever triages)
- Step 4: If model regression, flip traffic to validated fallback variant and lock model registry pin. (Owner: Research-oncall)
- Step 5: If resource saturation, trigger emergency capacity autoscale policy and open infra runbook. (Owner: infra-sre)

Rollback decision tree (condensed):
- Any red error-rate spike that persists > 5 minutes AND is not explained by a known short outage -> rollback to last stable release.
- Latency red that self-resolves within 3 minutes -> monitor; if not, rollback.
- Cost burn red alone (no errors/latency) -> throttle noncritical routes and engage finance-runbook.

Contingency runways (3 options to reduce user impact fast):
1) Route-level throttling: drop non-essential routes (analytics embeddings, low-priority batch jobs).
2) Model-tier fallback: route to smaller/cheaper model variant for best-effort users.
3) Regional failover: shift traffic to secondary region with capacity (must verify data residency before using).

Communication templates (copy/paste):
- Internal incident start: "INCIDENT: {route} experiencing elevated {metric}. Initial action: {action}. Current traffic level: {percent}. Owners: {owner list}."
- Customer-facing status: "We are aware of an issue affecting {subset of customers}. We have throttled new traffic to mitigate impact and are actively investigating. We'll provide updates every 15 minutes."

Open questions / TODOs (prior to signoff):
- Who owns rolling cost projections for a 72h unexpected surge? (finance + product-ops?). Assigned to Maya to coordinate.
- Validate that dedicated pools have independent autoscale budgets — infra-confirm by 2024-11-01.
- Add automated smoke validation that runs post-deploy in region A before enabling routing. (Engineering ticket: jira:PN-1123)

Post-launch 24h cadence (what to do after traffic reaches 100%):
- 0–6h: 10m checks on core signals, hourly summary notes to execs
- 6–24h: 30m checks, start trending anomalies to weekly tracker
- 24–72h: daily reviews + begin SLA credit review if any sustained degradation occurred

Retention & artifacts to attach after a roll:
- Canary runbook logs, perf snapshots, kv-cache dump (if safe), snapshots of pinned model registry
- Postmortem within 72h if any red gates fired and rolled back

Appendix: short checklist for preflight owners (tick before canary)
- [ ] Dashboards validated and shared to #launch-ops
- [ ] Oncall rotations confirmed for 72h window
- [ ] Canary script dry-run completed against staging
- [ ] Fallback model tested end-to-end (latency + correctness)
- [ ] Finance notified of expected burn profile and limit guards

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider an automated "soft hold" that reduces traffic by 10% on yellow triggers to buy human reaction time.
- Add a small synthetic customer cohort that receives ex-post prompts for quality validation — cheaper than full production evals.

If you edit this doc: add a short changelog line at the top with date and the delta. Keep the boarding sheet minimal — this is a fast reference for the ops desk, not a full runbook.

Changelog:
- 2024-10-03 Maya Chen: initial draft
- 2024-10-18 Priya Nair: added stress probes and probe owners
- 2024-11-01 Maya Chen: updated owners and added rolling cadence
